recipes.name: Balela Salad
ingredients_raw: 2 (15 ounce) cans garbanzo beans, drained and rinsed
2 (15 ounce) cans black beans, drained and rinsed
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Mix together garbanzo beans, black beans, mint, parsley, onion, and grape tomatoes in a large salad bowl until well combined.
Place jalapeño pepper, garlic, olive oil, lemon juice, and apple cider vinegar into a blender. Blend until dressing is thoroughly combined.
Pour dressing over salad and toss to mix. Sprinkle with salt and black pepper to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Balela Salad
raw_recipe.description: This balela is a quick Middle Eastern-style bean salad made with garbanzos, black beans, and lots of sweet grape tomatoes tossed in a tangy blender dressing.

review.reviewBody:
Like Lori, I came on here looking for Balela salad after trying it at Trader Joe's. I agree that this is far better, although theirs was good enough to inspire me to find a recipe!

I'm not normally an ingredient snob, but this recipe demands the best ingredients possible. Grape tomatoes generally have more flavor than typical store bought tomatoes, so that is not an area I would skimp on by using diced tomatoes (or egad! canned!). It takes a few extra minutes to half those grape tomatoes, but well worth it, in my view. 

Use the best olive oil you can find. I might roll my eyes at that suggestion in another recipe, but for this one, your choice of oil is going to make a difference. Trader Joe's California olive oil was my choice for this. It has a strong, fresh, peppery flavor that complements the other ingredients perfectly. 

I suggest you make it exactly as written before changing anything. The feta cheese suggestion sounds tempting, but this recipe is so well balanced I would hesitate to modify anything. Perhaps offer it on the side?

This salad is delicious. I really enjoyed the dressing. Made this for lunch for the week. I kept the components separate in the fridge and put together the night before. Did not add dressing (2tbsp) until right before eating. After the first day, I did add quinoa to it so it would be more filling. This will definitely be part of our regular lunch rotation.

Very easy to make! Topped it with shrimp for extra protein too. May try basil instead of the mint next time too! Could even see switching the onion to red onion. I made of the dressing for marinade for the shrimp and any other salads I make this week!

I recently took this to a potluck picnic at a winery. It was gone quickly, everyone loved it. I skipped the onion as I am not a fan of raw onion, and it wasn't missed. I substituted a serrano chile pepper as my jalepeno was very mild, and I did serve feta on the side as an option as Kevin suggested. The feta was a nice complement. I did like having it on the side as I think it could have gotten a bit liquified if it was in the salad all day. I also used fresh herbs and spices and good olive oil. It was a huge hit, everyone asked for the recipe. This is easy to pull together and a crowd pleaser.

I have had this ear-marked for some time now. Opted to make it today knowing I didn't have fresh mint on hand. I used dried mint. The changes I made: I reduced the amount of vinegar as I am not a lover of a strong vinegar taste and I salted the bean mixture; instead of the dressing mixture. Changes I will make in the future: I will use red onion instead of yellow onion, definitely fresh mint, and I will probably added either black olives or kalamata olives. Other reviews suggested avocado, corn, feta, etc....all good options as well. A keeper in my kitchen!

Originally found this salad at Trader Joes and loved it. This one is easy to make and is actually better. Added 1 can quartered artichoke hearts in water, drained and then chopped. Chopped the jalapeño and added directly to salad as well. Missed the part where you are supposed to blend it with the evoo, acv and lemon juice. Will try it again with the blended dressing and see if that helps to bring out the jalapeño flavor. This is a nutritious and flavorful salad. Excellent for meal by itself or for a side with your choice of protein. Great for potlucks too.

I came looking for this recipe after tasting a sample (and ultimately purchasing some) at Trader Joe's. I love the summery freshness of this salad and it's even better the next day after the flavors have a chance to meld. You definitely want to use fresh, not dried, parsley and mint. I liked the combination of the apple cider vinegar and lemon juice for the vinaigrette; however, I added a little liquid stevia (stevia is very concentrated so use cautiously) to balance the tartness. You could also use sugar or honey if you're not diabetic. As a matter of personal preference I didn't use or miss the jalapeno pepper. I also substituted Campari tomatoes (but wouldn't used canned) instead of grape and about a teaspoon of the refrigerated garlic paste instead of garlic cloves because that's what I had on hand. I saw where some substituted another bean for the garbanzo but I think the texture of the garbanzo adds a lot to this recipe. Last of all I added about 4 oz. of feta cheese. THIS IS SO GOOD!! For a truly Mediterranean meal I've even happily eaten it for breakfast or brunch with sardines or leftover fish! It's light but very satisfying and palate pleasing.

My husband and I love this salad! He is very sensitive to anything spicy so the first time I made it, I left out the jalapeño and added a couple drops of hot sauce. It was good but lacked pizzazz. The second time I used chili infused olive oil in place of plain olive oil. It gave it the kick it needed but was not overtly spicy. Hubby was fine with it. I also added feta cheese. That just put it over the top!

Delicious and satisfying! Make sure to use fresh not dried herbs and fresh not canned tomatoes. I added a red bell pepper that i had sitting around and needed to be used. Gave it a nice punch of color! I also added a teaspoon of Sumac spice which is usually present in Mediterranean food.

I love this recipe! I definitely recommend! I added avocado, corn, basil, cilantro and less of the lemon and olive oil! I also used roma tomatoes instead of cherry. It was really good! Lots of salt & pepper! :)

I've made this recipe many times with a few alterations. I use the juice of one lemon. I use cilantro for parsley. I also add extra jalapeno or use a Serrano chili which adds more heat (for home use}. for company I don't add extra heat. If you want flavor but little heat use a Poblano chili

I found it had a few too many black beans in it. I think next time I will switch out one can of the black beans for an additional can of Garbanzos. I did happen to have Sumac on hand from some other recipe, so I did add a teaspoon of that to the dressing. I feel like I added too much parsley (I didn't measure). Might cut back on that too next time. The taste is great, just too many black beans for my liking. Great potential here!
Made it twice in a week. Very VERY good! My bf accidentally grabbed a green pepper the first time instead of a jalapeño and I just blended that up instead. Great both ways! Very healthy too 💋
Bought this at Trader Joe’s & loved it but it was pricey so I found this recipe! I added a red, yellow & orange pepper! Yummy!
Loved the taste of it. I forgot to buy a jalapeño, so subbed 1/4-1/2 t. red pepper flakes.

I got quite excited about the ingredients and made it well enough in advance so the flavours would have time to mingle. I tossed it again before we ate and all I can say is lacklustre. I don't know how you can go wrong with the directions. Even the next day it still was lacking. Not one to waste food, my husband wouldn't help me finish it off the next day! Lol!
I didn't have mint or parsley so I used cilantro and I added cauliflower. I chopped all of it in my food processor.

I have made this salad several times following the recipe as written. It is a hit with my family and I will be making it many more times. It is really good on top a regular garden salad. Plus, it is very pretty!
Followed the recipe and it was amazing!!
The best dressing! Wow. I to substitute 1 can of black with a can of red beans and added a couple of stalks of celery.
